For the first time ever, I feel like I can trust AI to be my project manager... for basically everything.

Now that I have agents working in the background 24/7, with context + plugins connected to my entire company... I’m able to relax and focus on the task at hand.

I work with six different agencies that operate across different channels, Slack, email, Notion, text, WhatsApp, ClickUp, and more. It used to absolutely drain me to keep track of everything...

But now, I have AI keeping track of it all. And I’m slowly giving it the ability to respond to specific types of emails and Slack messages without asking for permission.

Every night, it adds all of that context to an internal company brain, which is basically one giant Notion database... the docs for my entire company.

I can plug any agent into this system. Then, every month, I have a mega-prompt where Fable 5 goes through everything, trims the fat, and gets rid of duplicates before I manually review it.

It’s like my monthly company review. It focuses on SOPs and company goals, and then I manually write my goal for the next month... which helps guide responses from every agent.

In summary:

1. Give your agents context on your entire company
2. Constantly remind your agents of your goals
3. Slowly give them more freedom to take action
4. Do a monthly review with the most powerful model available to realign everything
In most cases yes. Build products for agents.

text:
Ok so I’m starting to wrap my head around AI agents for knowledge work teams.

I’m realizing everyone will want an app like Codex/GPT work for individual use, as well as an agent they can use collaboratively. 

What the 2nd one looks like is unclear. 

Every company is different in size, the way they communicate, and what they do. It makes it hard to create a one size fits all “agent solution”… 

Setting up slack agents is hard but it’s not the hardest part. It’s the maintenance, permissions and the onboarding of new team members so they understand how to use the company agent. Also evals, models, skills, connections, channels, internal docs, versions, bugs and like 50 other things. 

If you’re a company that has a great setup for agents that your whole team uses, I would love to hear about it.
